site.name: Bitty
site.description: Tiny games and apps on small hardware. A growing side project by Ryan Grams, born from a questionable summer-camp idea.
site.story: I wanted to build a game device small enough for my kids to sneak into summer camp. We definitely got caught. The project kept growing anyway.
site.intro: Bitty grew into a home for some of our favorite games, ported to hardware that fits in your palm.
site.approachHeading: Built around tilt and a few buttons.
site.approachText: Porting a favorite to a screen this small means rethinking how it plays. I wanted tilting the device and tapping its few buttons to feel fun on their own.

budget.note: The device budget I had in mind. Prices vary by model and retailer. The optional controller is sold separately.

hero.alt: Two translucent orange M5Stick devices matching the supplied Plus SE reference, with illustrative Galaga and Flappy Bird screens.
hero.caption: Galaga + Flappy Bird
hero.label: Illustrative screen mockups
hero.note: Illustrative game screens. Public starter artwork differs. The mockups use a Plus SE shell. The original Plus is tested; SE support remains unverified.

installation.note: The source and installer preview are public on GitHub. Installation and firmware downloads are disabled while the first physical USB load is checked.

devices.name: Original M5StickC Plus
devices.description: This is the little orange device I’ve tested. It has a 135 × 240 screen, buttons and an onboard motion sensor. M5Stack now lists it as end of life, so check the exact model before hunting one down.

devices.name: StickC-Plus SE
devices.description: A candidate for button-based games. The SE removes the onboard motion sensor, so tilt controls need a different plan. It needs its own Bitty build and testing.

devices.name: M5StickS3
devices.description: A separate StickS3 build now compiles. Controls, audio, Bluetooth and sleep still need checks on real hardware. Physical compatibility remains unverified.

controller.name: IINE Gamebrick Mini (Grey)
controller.description: The controller I’ve tested pairs in H mode with its yellow indicator. Pairing, reconnecting, directions, rotation and running jumps have been checked on the original Plus. Other modes and controllers still need testing.
controller.headline: Itty bitty. IINE Mini.
controller.story: I wanted to play some of these with a physical controller, too. It still had to be itty bitty, so I went with the IINE Mini.

games.name: Galaga
games.description: Our Galaga adaptation uses original code and graphics. Tilt left or right to move, then tap or hold the front M5 button to fire. Controller directions and A/B are implemented. Physical play-testing for this game is still pending.

games.name: Flappy Bird
games.description: Tap the front M5 button to flap, start or try again. Controller A does the same, and B opens the menu. This one uses a button, with no tilt input. The public source includes original starter art.

games.name: More favorites + file adapters
games.description: We’ve also been working on block-stacking games, NES cartridge adapters and more arcade favorites. Compatibility varies by file and build. Bring files you’re entitled to use and adapt.

games.name: Two-device play
games.description: Linked play between two devices is being explored. A complete two-device radio playthrough still needs testing.

concepts.name: Lights Out
concepts.alt: Original concept art: a tiny purple player moves between tents and trees, away from amber flashlight beams.
concepts.description: The camp is quiet. The flashlight beams are doing laps. Pick your way back to the tent while the cones of light sweep between trees. Getting greedy about one more step is the whole problem.
concepts.controls: Tilt to creep. Hold the front button to freeze behind cover. A button-only control option would let you step between lanes.
concepts.appeal: Short rounds, readable shadows and that very specific feeling of getting away with something for a few glorious steps.

concepts.name: Patch Panic
concepts.alt: Original concept art: violet and amber cables cross a small grid between matching sockets.
concepts.description: Connect the right ports on a tiny patch panel. Every cable uses precious space. One suspiciously unhelpful lead keeps finding a way into the wrong socket. Yes, I want to make a game about cable management.
concepts.controls: Tap the side button to pick a tile. Tap the front button to rotate its cable. Hold to test the circuit. A tilt option could move the cursor.
concepts.appeal: A pocket-size puzzle with a clean little payoff when the whole signal path lights up.
